mainTopic: Whether an ערל may eat מעשר שני, רבי יצחק's 'ממנו' גזירה שוה, and the source that all טמאים are barred from תרומה.
overview: The גמרא asks whether an ערל (an uncircumcised man) may eat מעשר שני. It first shows that a תנא's list is not always complete, so leaving the ערל out of a list proves nothing. Several ברייתות are then brought as proofs. Each is pushed off: the מעשר they mention could be מעשר ראשון following רבי מאיר, or the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who treats an ערל like a טמא. Next the גמרא shows that רבי יצחק forbids an ערל from eating מעשר through a גזירה שוה on the word 'ממנו', shared by פסח and מעשר. To make that comparison hold, the גמרא shows that 'ממנו' is extra in the פסוקים, explaining every 'ממנו' by פסח and by מעשר, including ריש לקיש's teaching that impure מעשר שני may be used for anointing. Finally, the גמרא moves to the משנה's rule that all טמאים may not eat תרומה and begins רבי ישמעאל's source, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The list was not complete, so a תנא can leave things out
steps.stepSummary: The quoted source finishes with more differences between תרומה/ביכורים and מעשר that the earlier list did not mention. The גמרא concludes that the תנא left things out.
steps.simpleTranslation: They apply in all the years of the seven-year cycle, and they cannot be redeemed. That is not true of מעשר. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a source that names extra differences between תרומה and מעשר, then concludes that the earlier list was not complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there are differences the earlier list did not mention, the list was not meant to be complete. So the fact that ערל was missing from that list proves nothing about whether an ערל may eat מעשר. The גמרא looks for other evidence starting in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The years of the seven-year שמיטה cycle
Redemption: exchanging holy produce for money so the produce becomes ordinary
Tithe. Here it means מעשר שני, which is eaten in ירושלים
Learn from it: a conclusion formula

steps.whatToRemember: A תנא's list is not always complete, so leaving something out of a list does not prove anything.

phrases.english: And they apply in all the other years of the seven-year cycle,
and they have no redemption.
which is not so with tithe.
Learn from it.
phrases.notes: Learn that the תנא left items out of his list.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion about whether the תנא listed every difference.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תנא did not list every difference, so the missing case of ערל proves nothing.

steps.title: A ברייתא about leftover shreds of flesh after a מילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a man whose מילה is incomplete may not eat תרומה, פסח, קדשים, or מעשר. It suggests that this means מעשר דגן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: if shreds remained on him that hold back the מילה, he may not eat תרומה, the פסח, קדשים, or מעשר. Doesn't this mean produce tithe?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its open question and brings a ברייתא that seems to answer it: an incompletely circumcised man may not eat מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone with ציצין that hold back the מילה counts as an ערל. If the word מעשר in the ברייתא means produce tithe (מעשר שני), then an ערל may not eat מעשר שני, and the question is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Shreds of skin left after a מילה
That hold back: they make the מילה invalid
Tithe of grain or produce (מעשר שני)
Is it not? It proposes a reading that would prove the point

phrases.english: Come hear:
If shreds of flesh remained on him
that invalidate the circumcision,
this man may not eat
not תרומה, and not the Paschal lamb,
and not sacrificial food, and not tithe.
Is it not referring to tithe of produce?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that leaving something out of a list proves nothing, the גמרא looks for direct evidence.
steps.raayaObject: That an ערל may not eat מעשר שני.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about ציצין המעכבין that lists מעשר among the foods forbidden to him.

steps.title: No, the ברייתא means animal tithe
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. The מעשר in the ברייתא is מעשר בהמה, not produce tithe.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means animal tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the proof by reading the word מעשר as animal tithe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר בהמה is a קרבן, so of course an ערל may not eat it. Read this way, the ברייתא says nothing about produce tithe, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal tithe: every tenth animal, brought as a קרבן

phrases.english: No, it is animal tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא — מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the ברייתא proposed in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the identification of which מעשר is meant.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that מעשר meant produce tithe, but it could mean animal tithe.

steps.title: But animal tithe is already one of the קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the push-off. מעשר בהמה is a type of קדשים, which the ברייתא already lists, so listing it again would be pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: Animal tithe is the same as קדשים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 3. It points out that the ברייתא already said קדשים, and animal tithe is one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא does not normally repeat itself. If מעשר meant animal tithe, it would already be covered by the word קדשים. So מעשר should mean something new, namely produce tithe.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as
Sacrificial food: the meat of קרבנות

phrases.english: Animal tithe is the same as sacrificial food!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה הַיְינוּ קָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the push-off in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of מעשר as מעשר בהמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading makes the ברייתא repeat itself, since קדשים already includes animal tithe.

steps.title: The ברייתא already lists פסח and also קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends the push-off. The ברייתא already lists פסח and then also lists קדשים, so it clearly sometimes names a specific קרבן next to the general category.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic, didn't we learn פסח, and it also teaches קדשים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to the same ברייתא. It lists פסח, which is a קרבן, alongside קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If naming one particular קרבן next to קדשים is a problem, the same problem already exists with פסח. So the ברייתא might also name מעשר בהמה separately.

keyTerms.meaning: And by your reasoning: turning the challenger's logic back on him
Didn't we learn?
And it still teaches

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
didn't we learn the Paschal lamb,
and it also teaches sacrificial food!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the reading from step 3 against the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel case: the same text already lists a specific item next to its category.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing animal tithe next to קדשים makes the ברייתא repeat itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא already does this with פסח, so doing it with מעשר בהמה is no proof that something else is meant.

steps.title: פסח and קדשים are both needed, but animal tithe is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. Each of פסח and קדשים is needed for its own reason, but nothing explains why animal tithe would need to be listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, פסח and קדשים are both needed. If it only said פסח, I would think that only applies because ערלות is written about פסח, but not about קדשים. If it only said קדשים, I would think it means the פסח. But why would I need animal tithe?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why listing both פסח and קדשים makes sense, and then shows that the same reasons do not apply to animal tithe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה writes the ערל rule explicitly only about פסח, so each word was needed to prevent a different mistake. Animal tithe has no such special reason to be named. So the question returns, and מעשר in the ברייתא looks like produce tithe again.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted: this part makes sense
They are both needed
Being uncircumcised
I would have thought: a mistaken first assumption
Why do I need it?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא has decided the ברייתא means produce tithe. It has only shown that the animal-tithe answer is weak, and the discussion continues after this.

phrases.english: Granted, the Paschal lamb and sacrificial food are both necessary,
for if it had taught only the Paschal lamb,
I would say that is because lack of circumcision is written regarding the Paschal lamb,
but for sacrificial food, I would say no.
And if it had taught only sacrificial food, I would have said:
What is meant by sacrificial food? The Paschal lamb.
But animal tithe, why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא פֶּסַח וְקָדָשִׁים צְרִיכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison in step 5 and brings back the challenge from step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between פסח and מעשר בהמה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each of פסח and קדשים has its own reason to be listed, but animal tithe has none.
steps.whyThisMatters: The animal-tithe reading is now weak, so the ברייתא may still prove that an ערל may not eat מעשר שני.

steps.title: A new push-off: the tithe is first tithe, following רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: Since the animal-tithe answer failed, the גמרא says the מעשר in the ברייתא is מעשר ראשון, following רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא means first tithe, and it follows רבי מאיר, who said first tithe is forbidden to non-לויים.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier push-off (animal tithe) fell apart, so the גמרא gives a different way to push off the proof from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that מעשר ראשון is off-limits to ordinary Jews who are not לויים. So it makes sense that an ערל is also forbidden from eating it. That tells us nothing about מעשר שני, which any ordinary Jew may eat, so the proof is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: First tithe, given to the לויים
Literally 'strangers': people outside the group the food belongs to (here, non-לויים)
Rather; switching to a different answer

phrases.english: Rather, it is first tithe,
and it follows Rabbi Meir,
who said: first tithe is forbidden to non-Levites.
phrases.notes: Here 'זרים' means regular Jews who are not לויים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן, וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the animal-tithe push-off, which step 6 knocked down
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא in step 2
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The מעשר could be מעשר ראשון under רבי מאיר, which says nothing about מעשר שני

steps.title: New proof: an uncircumcised man is forbidden in two tithes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי חייא בר רב מדפתי says an ערל is forbidden in two tithes. The גמרא suggests these are produce tithe and animal tithe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי חייא בר רב of Difti taught that an ערל is forbidden in two tithes. Doesn't that mean produce tithe and animal tithe?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to prove that an ערל may not eat מעשר דגן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'two' tithes seems to point to two different kinds: one from produce and one from animals. If one of them is produce tithe, then an ערל is forbidden in מעשר דגן.

keyTerms.meaning: Two tithes
What, is it not...? Suggests how to read a source

phrases.english: Come and hear,

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִדִּפְתִּי:
phrases.english: from what Rabbi Chiyya bar Rav of Difti taught:
An uncircumcised man is forbidden in two tithes.
What, is it not

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן וְאֶחָד מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה!
phrases.english: one is produce tithe and one is animal tithe!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, מִדְּתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִדִּפְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was pushed off, a new source is brought
steps.raayaObject: That an ערל is forbidden in מעשר דגן
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי חייא בר רב מדפתי: an ערל is forbidden in two tithes

steps.title: Same push-off: first tithe, following רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers this proof the same way: the ברייתא is about מעשר ראשון and follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it means first tithe, and it follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the new proof using the same answer it just gave in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The produce tithe in this ברייתא can be מעשר ראשון, which רבי מאיר forbids to anyone who is not a לוי. So again there is no proof about מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too; the same answer works here

phrases.english: Here too,
it is first tithe, and it follows Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer from step 7 against the proof in step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי חייא בר רב מדפתי's ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The produce tithe there can be מעשר ראשון under רבי מאיר

steps.title: Proof from a list that leaves out the uncircumcised man
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists what an אונן, a טבול יום, and a מחוסר כפורים may and may not do. The גמרא argues that if an ערל could eat מעשר, the ברייתא should have listed him too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: an אונן is forbidden in מעשר but permitted in תרומה and the פרה אדומה. A טבול יום is forbidden in תרומה but permitted in the פרה and מעשר. A מחוסר כפורים is forbidden in the פרה but permitted in תרומה and מעשר. If an ערל may eat מעשר, the ברייתא should also teach: an ערל is forbidden in תרומה but permitted in the פרה and מעשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with three cases. It argues from what the ברייתא does not say: it never mentions an ערל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person in the list is forbidden in one thing and permitted in the other two. If an ערל could eat מעשר, he would fit this same pattern: forbidden in תרומה but permitted in the פרה and מעשר. The ברייתא could easily have listed him, so leaving him out suggests an ערל is forbidden in מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the day a close relative died, before burial
Someone who immersed today but is not fully pure until nightfall
Someone who still has to bring his atonement קרבן
The פרה אדומה (red heifer) and its preparation
If it were so, let it teach; a proof from what is missing

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מעשר' means מעשר שני, the tithe an owner eats in ירושלים. It is not first tithe.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
An acute mourner is forbidden in tithe,
and permitted in terumah and the heifer.
One who immersed that day is forbidden in terumah,
and permitted in the heifer and tithe.
One lacking atonement is forbidden in the heifer,
and permitted in terumah and tithe.
And if it is so,
let it teach: an uncircumcised man is forbidden in terumah,
and permitted in the heifer and tithe!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא — נִיתְנֵי: עָרֵל אָסוּר בַּתְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third attempt at a proof, after the 'two tithes' proof was pushed off
steps.raayaObject: That an ערל is forbidden in מעשר שני
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא listing אונן, טבול יום, and מחוסר כפורים, which leaves out an ערל

steps.title: This list follows רבי עקיבא, who treats the uncircumcised like an impure person
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. The ברייתא comes from the school of רבי עקיבא, who learns from 'איש איש' that an ערל is treated like a טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא comes from the school of רבי עקיבא, who includes an ערל in the rules of a טמא. As it is taught: רבי עקיבא says, 'איש איש' comes to include the ערל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ערל is missing from the list. That ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא's opinion, so it proves nothing for us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, an ערל is like a טמא. רש"י explains that this school forbids him in the פרה too, so the ברייתא could not list him as 'permitted in the פרה'. That is why it leaves him out, and it tells us nothing about מעשר. It only shows רבי עקיבא's view, and other תנאים may disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי עקיבא
Includes, learned from an extra word in a פסוק
Like a ritually impure person
Literally 'a man, a man'; the doubled word is used to include more people

steps.whatToRemember: Every attempt in this section to prove that an ערל is forbidden in מעשר שני has been pushed off. The answers were מעשר ראשון following רבי מאיר, and a ברייתא following רבי עקיבא's view that an ערל is like a טמא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common move in the גמרא: a source that seems to prove a point can be explained as following one particular תנא's opinion.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא — דְּבֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא,
phrases.english: This tanna is from the school of Rabbi Akiva,
who includes the uncircumcised man as being like an impure person.
As it is taught: Rabbi Akiva says:
"Any man" comes to include the uncircumcised man.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא — דְּבֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes off the proof from what is missing in step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא that leaves out the ערל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who treats an ערל like a טמא and so forbids him in מעשר. The omission reflects only his view, not that of the תנאים who disagree with him.

steps.title: Who disagrees with the school of רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא argues with רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the תנא that disagrees with רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 11 said the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא's school. Now the גמרא asks who the other side is, and this question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's school treats an ערל like a טמא, and in step 10's ברייתא it also restricts a מחוסר כפורים. If some תנא disagrees with that school, then according to that תנא an ערל might be allowed to eat מעשר. The גמרא wants to find that opposing תנא in a real source.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period, or the author of a teaching
Disagrees

phrases.english: And who is the תנא
who disagrees with רבי עקיבא?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer of step 11 by looking for the opposing opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of a תנא who argues with the school of רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: The first תנא in the argument about burning the פרה אדומה
steps.stepSummary: The opposing תנא is the first תנא who argues with רבי יוסף הבבלי. That תנא allows a מחוסר כפורים to burn the פרה אדומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the תנא who argues with רבי יוסף הבבלי, as a ברייתא teaches: if an אונן or a מחוסר כפורים burns the פרה אדומה, it is valid. רבי יוסף הבבלי says that if an אונן burns it, it is valid, but if a מחוסר כפורים burns it, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the opposing view belongs to the first תנא of a ברייתא about burning the פרה אדומה. That תנא allows even a מחוסר כפורים to do the burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's school restricts a מחוסר כפורים, and so does רבי יוסף הבבלי. The first תנא allows him, so he clearly disagrees with that school. The point is that a sage who argues with רבי עקיבא on this may also argue with him about an ערל.

keyTerms.meaning: The burning of the פרה אדומה (red heifer)
Valid
Invalid

steps.confusionAlert: The answer is not רבי יוסף הבבלי himself. He agrees with רבי עקיבא's school about the מחוסר כפורים. The one who disagrees is the first, unnamed תנא who argues with him.

phrases.english: It is the תנא who argues with רבי יוסף הבבלי.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word 'רבי' in round brackets. Either way, it's the sage who argues with רבי יוסף הבבלי.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
If an אונן or a מחוסר כפורים burns the heifer, it is valid.
רבי יוסף הבבלי says:
If an אונן burns it, it is valid,
if a מחוסר כפורים burns it, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵף הַבַּבְלִי הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first תנא of the ברייתא about burning the פרה אדומה is the one who argues with the school of רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רבי יצחק learns from 'ממנו' that an ערל may not eat מעשר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק also holds that an ערל may not eat מעשר. He learns it from a גזירה שוה on the word 'ממנו', which appears both by מעשר and by פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק also holds that an ערל is forbidden to eat מעשר. He said: from where do we know this? 'ממנו' is said about מעשר, and 'ממנו' is said about פסח. Just as an ערל may not eat the פסח, so too he may not eat מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another sage, רבי יצחק, who agrees that an ערל may not eat מעשר. It shows his source from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says clearly that an ערל may not eat the קרבן פסח. רבי יצחק links מעשר to פסח because the same word, 'ממנו', appears in both. This is a גזירה שוה, so the איסור for פסח carries over to מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Of it', the shared word used for the comparison
A comparison between two topics based on the same word appearing in both
The קרבן פסח (Pesach offering)
From where do we know?

phrases.english: And רבי יצחק also holds
that an ערל is forbidden to eat מעשר,
as רבי יצחק said:
From where do we know that an ערל is forbidden to eat מעשר?
'Of it' is said about מעשר,
and 'of it' is said about the פסח.
Just as with the 'of it' said about the פסח,
an ערל is forbidden to eat it,
so too with the 'of it' said about מעשר,
an ערל is forbidden to eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי יִצְחָק סָבַר עָרֵל אָסוּר בְּמַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another sage who holds that an ערל may not eat מעשר, and shows his source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ערל may not eat מעשר, learned from a גזירה שוה of 'ממנו' with פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a source in the פסוקים for the view that an ערל may not eat מעשר.

steps.title: The word must be free, or the comparison could be challenged
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the word 'ממנו' must be free (מופנה). Otherwise one could object that פסח is more severe, since one gets כרת for eating it as פיגול, נותר, or while טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word must be free. If it were not free, one could object: what is special about פסח is that one is liable for it because of פיגול, נותר, and טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a weak spot in רבי יצחק's גזירה שוה. It says the word must be 'free', and it shows the objection that would apply if it were not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal גזירה שוה can be broken if one side has a special strictness. פסח carries כרת for פיגול, נותר, and eating while טמא, so maybe that strictness is the reason an ערל is barred. The comparison only holds if the word 'ממנו' is extra in its own place, and therefore 'free' for the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Free': an extra word not needed in its own place, so it can be used for a גזירה שוה
To refute, to point out a difference that breaks the comparison
A קרבן ruined by a wrong intention about when it will be eaten
Meat of a קרבן left over past its time

steps.confusionAlert: 'מוּפְנֵי' does not mean 'turned away'. It means the word is 'free' for the comparison because it is not needed for anything else.

phrases.english: It must be free.
phrases.notes: The word 'ממנו' has to be extra where it's written, so it's free to be used for the comparison.

phrases.english: For if it were not free,
one could refute it:
What is special about the פסח?
That one is liable for it
because of פיגול, נותר, and being טמא.
phrases.notes: The liability here is כרת. That shows פסח is more severe than מעשר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּפְנֵי, דְּאִי לָא מוּפְנֵי אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a condition on רבי יצחק's גזירה שוה from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's גזירה שוה between פסח and מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פסח is stricter, since it carries כרת for פיגול, נותר, and טומאה. So the ban on an ערל might come from that strictness and not carry over to מעשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גזירה שוה works only if 'ממנו' is מופנה.

steps.title: The word is indeed free
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that 'ממנו' really is free, so the objection does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the objection does not apply: it is truly free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the concern from step 15. The word is in fact free, so the comparison stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because 'ממנו' is extra, the comparison is a firm one, and the difference that פסח is stricter cannot break it. The גמרא has not yet shown which 'ממנו' is extra, so it asks that next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is truly free

phrases.english: No, it is truly free.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאיֵי אַפְנוֹיֵי מוּפְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the possible objection raised in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the word is free, so the objection does not apply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison could be broken because פסח is stricter.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ממנו' is free, so the גזירה שוה holds.

steps.title: Which 'ממנו' is the free one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which 'ממנו' is free.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one is free?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof that 'ממנו' is really extra. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 only claimed the word is free. Now the גמרא wants to see in the פסוקים which 'ממנו' is not needed for its own teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: What, or which

phrases.english: Which one is free?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מוּפְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of the claim made in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which 'ממנו' is extra and therefore available for the גזירה שוה.

steps.title: Three times 'ממנו' is written about פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבא in the name of רבי יצחק says 'ממנו' appears three times about פסח. One is for its own teaching, one is for the גזירה שוה, and one is for something else. Steps 19 and 20 explain the third one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רבי יצחק: 'ממנו' is written three times about פסח. One is for its own teaching, one is for the גזירה שוה, and one is for...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers in the name of רבי יצחק that the פסוקים about פסח say 'ממנו' three times. The third use is explained in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'ממנו' appears three times, one use teaches its own simple meaning, and one is free for the גזירה שוה with מעשר. The third use gets its own purpose, which the גמרא explains next.

keyTerms.meaning: Three
For itself, for its own plain teaching
Are written

phrases.english: רבא said in the name of רבי יצחק:
'Of it' is written three times about the פסח:
one is for itself,
and one is for the גזירה שוה,
and one is for...

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק תְּלָתָא מִמֶּנּוּ כְּתִיבִי בְּפֶסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There are three 'ממנו's by פסח, so one of them is free for the גזירה שוה.

steps.title: The third 'ממנו' by פסח, according to the first view
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that the פסוק adds a positive command after a prohibition, the third 'ממנו' is written only because the word 'נותר' is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the verse comes to give a positive command (burning the leftovers) after a prohibition (not leaving leftovers), the word 'of it' is written only because the word 'that which remains' is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third 'ממנו' by פסח, which was left open at the end of step 18. According to this view, it does not teach anything new. It is simply part of the phrase that comes along with 'נותר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view says the פסוק 'והנותר ממנו עד בקר באש תשרפו' is there to add a עשה after the לא תעשה of 'ולא תותירו'. That purpose needs the word 'נותר'. 'ממנו' is just written along with it, so it is not needed for a separate teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive command that comes after a prohibition
Since; because (it is written along with something else)
Leftover sacrificial meat

phrases.english: According to the one who says:
the verse comes to give you
a positive command after a prohibition —
phrases.notes: The prohibition is not leaving the פסח until morning. The positive command is burning whatever was left over.

phrases.english: since 'that which remains' is written,
'of it' is also written.

steps.triggerLanguage: למאן דאמר בא הכתוב ליתן לך עשה אחר לא תעשה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from step 18 by explaining the third 'ממנו'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the third 'ממנו' by פסח for?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is written only because the word 'נותר' is written next to it.

steps.title: The third 'ממנו' by פסח, according to the second view
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that the פסוק teaches a 'second morning' for burning, the third 'ממנו' is written only because 'עד בקר' is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says the verse comes to give it a second morning for burning, the word 'of it' is written only because 'until morning' is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of explanation according to the other view about this פסוק. Here too, the third 'ממנו' is only written along with other words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view reads the פסוק as teaching that the leftovers are burned on a later morning, not on יום טוב. That teaching depends on the words 'עד בקר'. 'ממנו' just comes along with them, so it is not needed for its own teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: A second morning
Burning

phrases.english: And according to the one who says
to give it a second morning for its burning —
since 'until morning' is written,
'of it' is also written.

steps.triggerLanguage: ולמאן דאמר ליתן לו בקר שני לשריפתו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the same explanation as step 19, according to the other view of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the third 'ממנו' by פסח for, according to the second view?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is written only because 'עד בקר' is written next to it.

steps.title: All three 'ממנו' words by מעשר are already used
steps.stepSummary: By מעשר, 'ממנו' appears three times: one for its own teaching, one for רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן, and one for ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Of it' is written three times regarding tithe: one for itself, one for the teaching of רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן, and one for the teaching of ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the other side of the גזירה שוה, the 'ממנו' words by מעשר. It shows that each one already has its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים 26:14 says 'ממנו' three times. Since all three are used for teachings, none of them is left free. So the free 'ממנו' for the גזירה שוה comes from the פסח side. The גמרא then explains the teaching of ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Tithe (here, מעשר שני)
For its own plain meaning
Three

phrases.english: Three 'of it's are written regarding tithe:
one for itself,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד לִדְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: and one for the teaching of Rabbi Abbahu in the name of Rabbi Yochanan,
and one for the teaching of Reish Lakish.

steps.triggerLanguage: תלתא ממנו כתיבי במעשר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the פסח side of the גזירה שוה to the מעשר side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All three 'ממנו' words by מעשר are used for other teachings.

steps.title: טמא מעשר שני may be used for anointing
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, in the name of רבי סימאי, learns from 'ולא נתתי ממנו למת' that טמא מעשר שני may be used for anointing.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי סימאי: From where do we know that מעשר שני that became impure may be used to anoint oneself? Because it says, 'Nor did I give of it for the dead.' I did not give it for the dead, but for the living in the same way as for the dead, I did give. What use is the same for the living and the dead? That is anointing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings ריש לקיש's teaching, which is the job of the third 'ממנו' by מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says the מעשר was not given 'למת', for the dead. That implies it may be given to the living in the same way it would be given to the dead. Anointing is something done both for the living and for the dead, so that is the permitted use.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים
Anointing the body with oil
Similar to; in the same way as
You must say

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר רַבִּי סִימַאי:
phrases.english: As Reish Lakish said that Rabbi Simai said:
From where do we know that second tithe that became impure
may be used to anoint oneself —
as it is said: 'Nor did I give of it for the dead.'
It is for the dead that I did not give,
but for the living, in the same way as for the dead — I did give.
What is something that is the same for the living and the dead?
You must say: this is anointing.

steps.triggerLanguage: דאמר ריש לקיש אמר רבי סימאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the teaching of ריש לקיש that step 21 mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טמא מעשר שני may be used for anointing, learned from 'ולא נתתי ממנו למת'.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means buying a coffin and shrouds
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא challenges: maybe the פסוק is talking about buying a coffin and shrouds, not about anointing.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא objected: But say instead that the verse means buying a coffin and shrouds for him.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא attacks ריש לקיש's reading by offering a different meaning for 'למת'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe 'I did not give for the dead' means using מעשר money to buy a coffin and shrouds. If so, the matching permitted use for the living would be buying clothes, and the פסוק would say nothing about anointing.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objected to it
Coffin
Burial shrouds

phrases.english: Mar Zutra objected to it:
But say it means to buy him a coffin and shrouds?

steps.triggerLanguage: מתקיף לה מר זוטרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 22 reads the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that 'למת' refers to anointing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another use that applies to the dead, buying a coffin and shrouds, could fit the פסוק just as well.

steps.title: 'ממנו' means from the מעשר itself
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers that 'ממנו' means from the מעשר itself, not from money exchanged for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: 'Of it' means from its own body.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers מר זוטרא from the word 'ממנו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ממנו' means using the actual מעשר. A coffin and shrouds would be bought with money, not made from the מעשר itself. Anointing uses the מעשר itself, so ריש לקיש's reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: From its own body; from the thing itself

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
'Of it' — from its own body.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר זוטרא's challenge from step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק could mean buying a coffin and shrouds with מעשר money.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ממנו' requires using the מעשר itself, which fits anointing.

steps.title: 'I did not give' matches 'I did not eat'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers differently: 'לא נתתי' is like 'לא אכלתי'. Eating uses the מעשר itself, so giving must use the מעשר itself too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: 'I did not give' is like 'I did not eat'. Just as there it means from the tithe itself, so too here it means from the tithe itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second answer to מר זוטרא by comparing two phrases in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק says 'לא אכלתי באני ממנו', and eating is always done with the מעשר itself. So 'לא נתתי' must also mean using the מעשר itself, which excludes buying a coffin with money. This ends the challenge, and ריש לקיש's teaching stays as the job of the third 'ממנו'.

keyTerms.meaning: I did not give
I did not eat
Just as there, so too here (a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: Every 'ממנו' by מעשר is already used for a teaching. The third one teaches that טמא מעשר שני may be used for anointing, because 'ממנו' means from the מעשר itself.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
'I did not give' is like 'I did not eat':
phrases.notes: Both phrases are in the same פסוק, דברים 26:14.

phrases.english: just as there, it is from its own body —
so too here, it is from its own body.

steps.triggerLanguage: רב אשי אמר לא נתתי דומיא דלא אכלתי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the same challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison between phrases in the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Giving for the dead' could include buying things with מעשר money.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like eating, giving must be from the מעשר itself, so the פסוק refers to anointing.

steps.title: The analogy is free on only one side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the 'ממנו' גזירה שוה is free on only one side. That works for the view of למדין ואין משיבין, but not for the view of למדין ומשיבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is still a problem: the word is free on only one side. That is fine for the one who says we learn from such an analogy and cannot argue against it. But for the one who says we learn from it and can also argue against it, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem. The 'ממנו' by מעשר is already used up by רבי אבהו, so only the 'ממנו' by פסח is free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה that is free (מופנה) on only one side is weaker. One view says we can still learn from it and we may not knock it down with logic (למדין ואין משיבין). The other view says we can knock it down with logic (למדין ומשיבין), and earlier the גמרא showed that פסח and מעשר שני really are different.

keyTerms.meaning: Free, a word not needed for its own place, so it can be used for a גזירה שוה
From one side, only one of the two matching words is free
We learn from it, and we do not refute it with logic
We learn from it, but we may refute it with logic
This works out fine

steps.confusionAlert: Both views agree that you may learn from a one-sided גזירה שוה. The only argument is whether a logical difference between the two cases can knock it down.

phrases.english: And still, it is free on only one side.
phrases.notes: Only the 'ממנו' by פסח is free. The one by מעשר was already used for רבי אבהו (Step 21).

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says
we learn from it and do not refute it.
But for the one who says
we learn from it and we may refute it,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי מוּפְנֶה מִצַּד אֶחָד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the 'ממנו' of מעשר was assigned to רבי אבהו and ריש לקיש, the גמרא attacks the strength of the גזירה שוה itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שוה of 'ממנו' between פסח and מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the מעשר side is not free, the analogy is one-sided and can be refuted according to למדין ומשיבין.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's law comes from a different source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אבהו's law does not need 'ממנו'. It comes from רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That teaching of רבי אבהו comes from what רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem by moving רבי אבהו's law to a different פסוק. The next step brings that source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אבהו's law (that you may burn טמא תרומה) is learned from somewhere else, then the 'ממנו' by מעשר is not needed for it. That makes the word free by מעשר too, so the גזירה שוה is free on both sides and cannot be refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes out from, it is learned from
That one

phrases.english: That teaching of Rabbi Abbahu

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ נָפְקָא.
phrases.english: comes out from what Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָךְ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ מִדְּרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the one-sided objection of Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning a law to a different source, which frees up the word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'ממנו' by מעשר was needed for רבי אבהו, so the analogy was one-sided.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אבהו's law comes from another פסוק, so 'ממנו' is free on both sides.

steps.title: Two kinds of תרומה: pure and impure
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה learns from 'תרומתי' (plural) that the פסוק speaks of pure and impure תרומה. From 'לך' he learns that impure תרומה is yours to burn under your cooking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: What does it mean when it says, 'And I, behold, I have given you the charge of My terumot'? The פסוק is talking about two kinds of תרומה, pure תרומה and impure תרומה. The תורה says 'to you': it shall be yours, to burn under your cooking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source mentioned in Step 27. It explains a פסוק in במדבר to show that a כהן may get use from impure תרומה by burning it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural word 'תרומתי' shows two types of תרומה, pure and impure. 'לך' means the כהן may benefit from both. Impure תרומה cannot be eaten, so its benefit is burning it as fuel. This gives רבי אבהו's law a source without using 'ממנו'.

keyTerms.meaning: The charge of My terumot (plural)
Impure תרומה, which may not be eaten
Burning as fuel
A cooked dish
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that a כהן may burn impure תרומה and benefit from it. Because of it, the 'ממנו' גזירה שוה survives.
steps.whatToRemember: Because רבי אבהו's law comes from 'תרומתי… לך', the word 'ממנו' is free on both sides. So the גזירה שוה between פסח and מעשר cannot be refuted even by the view of למדין ומשיבין.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: As Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And I, behold, I have given you
the charge of My terumot"
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:8. Notice the word is plural, 'my terumot'.

phrases.english: the verse is speaking of two terumot:
one is pure teruma,
and one is impure teruma.
And the Merciful One said: "to you":
it shall be yours,
to burn beneath your cooked dish.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the source that Step 27 pointed to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From 'תרומתי… לך' we learn that impure תרומה belongs to the כהן and may be burned as fuel for cooking.

steps.title: Source for barring all impure people from תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that all טמאים may not eat תרומה and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And all the impure ones, etc.' Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the next line of the משנה and asks where the rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that anyone with any kind of טומאה may not eat תרומה. The גמרא wants a פסוק that covers every kind of טומאה, not just one type.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure people, those with טומאה
Where are these words learned from?

phrases.english: "And all the impure ones, etc."
From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הַטְּמֵאִים כּוּ׳ מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the 'ממנו' discussion and moves to a new line in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that every kind of טמא is forbidden to eat תרומה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's source from a leper and a זב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי ישמעאל, brings the פסוק about a כהן who is a צרוע or a זב. He begins to ask what these two have in common.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי ישמעאל: The פסוק says, 'Any man from the seed of Aaron who is a leper or a זב, etc.' What thing is the same...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer the question with a פסוק that names a צרוע and a זב. Then it starts to ask what these two share. The answer continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names only two kinds of טמאים. רבי ישמעאל is about to look for what they have in common, so that he can include all other kinds of טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת, a kind of skin affliction
A man with a certain bodily discharge that makes him impure
The descendants of אהרן, the כהנים

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
The verse states:
"Any man from the seed of Aaron
who is a leper or a zav, etc."
What matter is the same

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is 'איש איש מזרע אהרן והוא צרוע או זב', and from it we learn about all טמאים by finding what they have in common. The explanation continues past this point.
